title: WPMS/2684/2025 of DALIP SINGH Vs ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY LTD

paras.text:
2026:UHC:827
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR VERMA
12TH FEBRUARY, 2026
WRIT PETITON NO.2684 of 2025 (M/S)
Dalip Singh Adhikari .....Petitioner
Versus
Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. ....Respondent
Counsel for the Petitioner: Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia,
 Advocate holding brief of
 Mr. Altaf Hussain, Advocate.
Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma,J.
The petitioner had filed a Complaint
(Consumer Complaint No.281 of 2013, "Sh. Dalip Singh
Adhikari vs. The Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.
through its Principal Officer") before the National
Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, New Delhi
(in short, "Commission"). The Commission passed the
final order on 29.04.2025. The Commission, while
partially allowing the complaint, directed the opposite
party to pay the claim of Rs.1,28,61,082/- preferred by
the Complainant based on the estimate of the PWD
after deducting the amount of Rs.7,39,085/- paid
towards repairs for the entire stretch of the Rikhari-Bachham road and applicable deductions with simple
interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of
1

2026:UHC:827
the filing of the claim. The Commission further directed
that the said amount shall be paid within eight weeks'
of the order, failing which the applicable rate of interest
shall be 9% per annum till realization.
2. The present writ petition has been filed under
Article 227 of the Constitution of India with a prayer to
grant 18% interest instead of 6% interest awarded by
the Commission.
3. Heard Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, learned counsel
appearing for the petitioner, on the maintainability of
the writ petition.
4. Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate submitted
that the present writ petition is maintainable under
Article 227 of the Constitution of India. He has relied on
the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in
"Universal Sompo General Insurance Company
Limited vs. Suresh Chand Jain and Another,
(2024) 9 SCC 148".
5. The Hon'ble Supreme Court has considered
the question as to whether against the order passed by
the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission
in an appeal under Section 58(1)(a)(iii) of the
Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (in short, "Act, 2019"),
a writ petition before the High Court under Article 227
2

2026:UHC:827
of the Constitution of India would be maintainable?.
6. According to Mr. Hari Mohan Bhatia, Advocate,
the said complaint (Consumer Complaint No.281 of
2013) was filed directly before the Commission.
7. An order passed by the Commission in an
appeal under Section 58(1)(a) (iii) of the Act, 2019 can
be challenged before the High Court under Article 227
of the Constitution of India, but, the appeal against the
original order of the Commission must be filed before
the Hon'ble Supreme Court under Section 67 of the Act,
2019.
8. Therefore, this writ petition is not
maintainable. Accordingly, the writ petition is dismissed
as not maintainable.
 ___________________
ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.
Date: 12.02.2026
JKJ/Pant
